brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: Build is piece:0,0,0;half-n alone at level 0 with no neighboring pieces and no level 1 — one base only (half-n is the single-base variant that provides a cut face for a drawer).

Configurator offers 0 drawer sockets on a full hex base (find_sockets drawer =0). Notch drawers require an empty position beside two touching bases, bay drawers require three bases, both violate 'nothing beside'. The only drawer that respects the single-base constraint is the cut-face drawer on a half base, of which max 1 is offered (s79 -> drawer:0#0,0#cut). Five drawers inside one cell is not offered and was refused when attempted (SITE_FILLED). Build contains 1 drawer, not 5.

finish.summary: Restored single-base constraint (one half-n base at 0,0,0). Full base provides zero drawer sockets; the configurator only allows a drawer in a single base via its cut face (half base = 1 drawer). Notch/bay frames that could add more drawers need empty interstitial positions beside 2-3 bases, which would break the 'nothing beside or on top' rule and are not offered. Built the maximum allowed under the constraint — 1 drawer — and left four drawers unmet by the system's placement rules.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
